title: Bit Prefixes That Divide by Five
statement:
You get an array bits of 0s and 1s. For each index i, read bits[0..i] as a binary number with bits[0] as the most significant bit.

Return an array of booleans where entry i is true when that number is divisible by 5. The array can be long, so the numbers themselves get far too large for any integer type.

examples.why: 1, 3, 7, 15. Only 15 is a multiple of 5, though the last bit is the same as before.
Leading zeros give the value 0, which is divisible by 5.

hints: Appending a bit b to a number v gives 2·v + b. How does the remainder mod 5 change?
(2·v + b) mod 5 depends only on v mod 5, so you never need v itself.
Keep rem = (2·rem + bit) % 5 as you walk; the answer at each step is rem === 0.

explain.intuition:
Each new bit shifts the number left and adds the bit: v' = 2v + b. Remainders survive addition and multiplication, so v' mod 5 = (2 · (v mod 5) + b) mod 5. You only ever store a number from 0 to 4, no matter how many bits arrive.

The naive version keeps the full value. In JavaScript a number loses precision after 53 bits, and even BigInt makes every step slower as the number grows, which turns the whole scan into O(n²).
pitfalls: Keeping the full value in a normal number. After 53 bits it is no longer exact, and the answers are wrong.
Checking only the last bit or the last few bits. Divisibility by 5 depends on the whole number, not on a suffix.

complexity.space: O(1) extra, O(n) for the output

solutions.title: Big integers
solutions.idea: Build the exact value with BigInt and test it each step. Correct, but each step costs more as the number grows.

solutions.title: Running remainder
solutions.idea: Only the value mod 5 matters for the next step, so keep just that.

followups: The bits arrive least significant first. What do you track now?
Answer the same question for divisibility by any k. How many states does the remainder have?
